title: R=15 food-cog continuation replicates on fresh seed 3: shell band at r=12, trough at r=5 (1.5x of R=10), and a local food cut kills the cog by t=635 while its fed twin and all others stay at 1.00; but 10 cogs persist here, so the 'fewer persist' observation is seed-dependent
summary: Ran the finding's world.py unchanged with WORLD_P R=15 (288^2) on fresh seed 3: labkit pack to t=1000 (33 bodies at peak, 10 final, about 11 stable cogs from t~220 with none dying afterwards; pack_r15/sheet.png). Shell profile by the claim's radial_cog.py over 160 isolated cell-frames: A1 1.00 at the centre, 0.00 trough at r=5, shell 0.97 at r=12, 0.0004 at r=25-29. Fork with the claim's scripts (runsave to t=600, mkcut RAD=27: most isolated cog, nearest other core 73 px; fed twin vs food cut for 300 t): cut cog <10% at t=635 and 0.000 at t=900; fed twin 1.004; all other bodies 0.996 in both arms (localcut_r15.png/json), the same t=635 as the finding.

observations.B: radial_r15_seed3.png: shell 0.97 at r=12 between a 0.00 trough at r=5 and 0.0004 outside, 160/160 isolated cell-frames (R=10: r=7 and r=3)
observations.E: localcut_r15.png/json: cut cog <10% at t=635, fed twin 1.004, all others 0.996

seeds_run.result: pass: shell scales 1.5x; local cut kills the cog by t=635; 10 cogs persist to t=1000

controls_run.E: r15fed3 vs r15cutrun3 from the same t=600 checkpoint (localcut_r15.json)

by_construction: E (matter is built only from food)
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. On it cogs do not die spontaneously after t~260 (10 final, about 11 stable), unlike the finding's seeds 0 and 1 (3 and 6), so reduced persistence at R=15 is seed-dependent rather than general. dt was not halved.
